comments.body:
Cancellation audit (M174, 2026-07-15): work shipped via M169-rev (dogfood log Entry 31) with a different design than this milestone's AC text specifies.

What M174 specified vs what shipped:
- F-01 (HIGH, AC-01: "Tab on Settings preserves staged edits") — M174's design was to preserve. M169-rev shipped "Tab wraps + discards per AC-06" (the wrap makes Tab on Settings a leaving gesture, so AC-06 discard kicks in). These are mutually exclusive; the M169 AC-01 wrap text and AC-06 discard text both predate M174, and the M169-rev design keeps both contracts intact. Test: rev_high_tab_on_settings_wraps_and_clears_per_ac06.
- F-02 (MED, AC-02: "Staging `ui.color = yes` shows the coerced value `true` in the row buffer while editing") — M174's design was to read the coerced value back from `mp config set --dry-run`. M169-rev shipped "staging no longer mutates state.config" — the shadow is removed, but the in-memory row still shows the raw user string until save. Tests: rev_med_yes_for_bool_field_does_not_pollute_state_config, rev_med_save_with_yes_writes_bool_true_to_disk.
- F-03 (MED, AC-03: "apply_settings_save rolls back on partial failure") — M174's design was to write a pre-batch snapshot on rollback. M169-rev shipped "partial commit keeps failed key staged for retry" (track committed, drop them from staged_edits, keep the failed key staged so the user can fix and retry). Test: rev_med_partial_commit_failure_keeps_failed_key_staged.
- F-04 (LOW, AC-04: Tab wraps at ends) — shipped. Independent re-implementation in M198.
- F-05 (LOW, AC-05: staged_edits is BTreeMap) — shipped. Test: rev_low_staged_edits_iterate_in_key_sorted_order.

Why cancellation was the right call: the M169-rev design keeps the M169 AC-01 wrap + AC-06 discard contracts intact, both of which predate M174.
